subtitle: Hariraja’s Year of Fire: Ajmer Between Stone and Script

panels.shot: epic wide of Ajmer’s hill-fort at dusk, half in shadow, half in the red of the setting sun
panels.action: Hariraja stands on the battlements of Ajmer, mail-clad, hand on sword, staring down at the town where temple spires and freshly built arches of a new mosque share the skyline.

dialogue.text: 1192 CE. Prithviraj is gone. In Ajmer, his brother Hariraja fights for a single burning year, while Qutb al-Din Aibak’s masons turn a Sanskrit college into a mosque.

i18n.hi: ११९२ ईस्वी। पृथ्वीराज चला गया। अजमेर में उसका भाई हरिराज एक जलते साल तक लड़ता है, जबकि क़ुत्बुद्दीन ऐबक के राजमिस्त्री एक संस्कृत कॉलेज को मस्जिद में बदल देते हैं।

panels.shot: sweeping bird’s-eye over the battlefield of Tarain, littered with abandoned standards and riderless horses
panels.action: A dusty plain near Tarain lies scarred by war; broken lances, fallen banners of the Chahamanas and the Ghurids’ black standards jut from the earth under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: At Tarain in 1192, Muhammad of Ghor’s cavalry broke Prithviraj’s host. A kingdom that had held Delhi and Sambhar salt cracked in a single day.

i18n.hi: ११९२ में तराइन पर मोहम्मद ग़ोरी की सवारों ने पृथ्वीराज की फ़ौज तोड़ दी। दिल्ली और सांभर की नमक-दरबार सँभालने वाला राज एक ही दिन में चूर हो गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Ajmer’s fort and town, seen from the surrounding hills
panels.action: Ajmer’s high stone walls and crowded bazaar below nestle between rocky hills; caravans laden with salt wind along the roads, while smoke rises from temple courtyards.

dialogue.text: Ajmer, heart of Sapadalaksha, watched anxiously. Its salt caravans and hill fort were now prizes in a wider struggle between Rajput clans and the new Ghurid power.

i18n.hi: सपादलक्ष की धड़कन अजमेर चिन्तित देख रहा था। उसके नमक कारवाँ और पहाड़ी क़िला अब राजपूत कुलों और नई ग़ुरी ताक़त की बड़ी जंग के इनाम बन गए थे।

panels.shot: medium wide inside a Ghurid camp tent, low-angle on a throne chair and two figures in silhouette
panels.action: Inside a canvas pavilion, Muhammad of Ghor’s figure sits elevated, while beside him a younger Rajput prince stands respectfully, head bowed.

dialogue.text: Hasan Nizami later wrote that after Tarain, the Ghurid sultan set Prithviraj’s son Govindaraja at Ajmer as his vassal. The old center now had a new, precarious master.

i18n.hi: हसन निज़ामी ने लिखा कि तराइन के बाद ग़ुरी सुल्तान ने पृथ्वीराज के बेटे गोविन्दराज को अपना जागीरदार बना कर अजमेर में बिठाया। पुराना केंद्र अब नए, डगमग मालिक के हाथ था।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle medium on Hariraja in a torchlit hall, shadows sharp against stone pillars
panels.action: Hariraja stands tense in Ajmer’s audience hall, torchlight flickering on his face, jaw set, hand gripping the hilt of his sword as courtiers watch in uneasy silence.

dialogue.text: But Prithviraj had a brother. Hariraja could not accept Ajmer ruled by a son bound to the conqueror. Family loyalty and political survival pulled in opposite directions.

i18n.hi: पर पृथ्वीराज का एक भाई था। हरिराज अजमेर को उस बेटे के हाथ नहीं छोड़ सकता था जो विजेता का बंधुआ था। परिवार की निष्ठा और राज की जान अलग दिशाओं में खिंच रही थी।

panels.shot: sweeping wide inside Vigraharaja’s Sarasvati temple and college, with colonnades and carved slabs
panels.action: In a grand pillared hall, Hariraja walks between rows of carved stone slabs, their Sanskrit drama verses and figures glowing softly in lamplight as teachers and students bow.

dialogue.text: Ajmer’s pride was not only steel. Vigraharaja’s Sarasvati temple and Sanskrit college had filled these halls with verse and learning. Inscribed plays in stone lined the colonnades.

i18n.hi: अजमेर की शान सिर्फ़ लोहे में नहीं थी। विग्रहराज का सरस्वती मंदिर और संस्कृत कॉलेज इन दीवारों को कविता और विद्या से भरते थे। पत्थरों पर खुदी नाटकें बरामदों में सजी थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Hariraja’s face, half-lit, eyes resolute
panels.action: Hariraja looks straight ahead, brows knitted, as the light from a nearby lamp catches the edge of his cheek and the steel of his helmet.

dialogue.speaker: hariraja
dialogue.text: Ajmer is not a throne to be gifted. It is a trust I cannot surrender.

i18n.hi: अजमेर कोई बख़्शी हुई गद्दी नहीं। ये एक अमानत है, जिसे मैं नहीं छोड़ूँगा।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of palace courtyard, Hariraja’s troops rushing through gates as Govindaraja’s guards retreat
panels.action: In a tense courtyard, Hariraja strides forward with armed retainers, while a smaller group of Govindaraja’s men withdraw, looking back over their shoulders.

dialogue.text: Sources agree that Hariraja soon drove Govindaraja out and took Ajmer. A brief, sharp struggle decided which branch of Prithviraj’s line held the city.

i18n.hi: सभी स्रोत मानते हैं कि हरिराज ने जल्द ही गोविन्दराज को निकाल बाहर किया और अजमेर ले लिया। छोटी, तीखी जंग ने तय किया कि पृथ्वीराज की कौन सी शाखा शहर सँभालेगी।

panels.shot: high-angle wide on Ajmer’s ramparts, Hariraja overseeing frantic preparations
panels.action: On the battlements, Hariraja directs men hauling stones, stacking arrows and fixing shields, while messengers hurry and watchfires burn along the wall.

dialogue.text: By 1192–93, Hariraja ruled a besieged world. He strengthened Ajmer’s walls, rallied Chahamana feudatories, and tried to hold the salt trade that fed his revenue.

i18n.hi: ११९२–९३ तक हरिराज घिरे हुए जगत का राजा था। उसने अजमेर की दीवारें मज़बूत कीं, चाहमान जागीरदारों को जुटाया और आय देने वाले नमक व्यापार को सँभालने की कोशिश की।

panels.shot: wide shot of Qutb al-Din Aibak’s column advancing across the plains toward Ajmer
panels.action: On the open plain, Qutb al-Din Aibak rides at the head of a Ghurid column, horsemen in mailed ranks and foot archers marching behind, banners snapping in the wind.

dialogue.text: Minhaj-i-Siraj later recorded Qutb al-Din Aibak’s campaigns as the sultan’s arm in Hindustan. Now his column turned toward Ajmer, to end Hariraja’s resistance.

i18n.hi: मिन्हाज़-ए-सिराज़ ने बाद में क़ुत्बुद्दीन ऐबक की मुहिमों को हिंदुस्तान में सुल्तान का हाथ लिखा। अब उसकी फ़ौज अजमेर की ओर मुड़ी, हरिराज की बग़ावत ख़त्म करने।

panels.shot: tense medium on Hariraja in council with a few chiefs around a low table with a rough map
panels.action: Hariraja leans over a cloth map marked with stones, ringed by serious-faced chiefs; a small figurine marks Ajmer, with pebbles showing Ghurid forces converging.

dialogue.text: Hariraja’s choices narrowed. Fight in the open where Ghurid cavalry had already triumphed, or cling to Ajmer’s fort and hope allies would come in time.

i18n.hi: हरिराज के विकल्प सिमटते गए। खुले मैदान में लड़े जहाँ ग़ुरी सवार पहले ही जीत चुके थे, या अजमेर के क़िले से चिपक कर बैठे रहें और उम्मीद करें कि साथी समय पर पहुँचें।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of Ajmer’s walls during siege, arrows arcing, siege engines in the distance
panels.action: Ajmer’s high walls bristle with defenders loosing arrows, while below, Ghurid troops push siege equipment forward and horsemen wait, dust hanging in the air.

dialogue.text: That year became a test of stone against horse. Hariraja’s men hurled missiles from the ramparts; Aibak’s army tightened its grip, cutting supplies and routes.

i18n.hi: वो साल पत्थर और घोड़े की टक्कर बन गया। हरिराज के सैनिक बुर्जों से मिसाइलें बरसाते रहे; ऐबक की फ़ौज ने घेरा कस दिया, रसद और रास्ते काट दिए।

panels.shot: melancholic medium interior of the Sarasvati temple-college during siege, half-empty, teachers anxious
panels.action: Inside the pillared college hall, remaining scholars cluster around bundled manuscripts, glancing toward the doorway where the distant rumble of war reaches them.

dialogue.text: In the college halls, classes thinned. Some teachers fled; others stayed, unsure if Ajmer’s stone verses and manuscripts would survive the siege or be consumed by it.

i18n.hi: कॉलेज की दीर्घाओं में कक्षाएँ घट गईं। कुछ आचार्य भाग गए; कुछ टिके रहे, अनजान कि अजमेर के पत्थर पर खुदे श्लोक और पांडुलिपियाँ घेराबंदी में बचेंगी या उसी में जल जाएँगी।

panels.shot: somber wide of Ajmer’s gate opened, with Ghurid troops entering in ordered ranks
panels.action: The great gate of Ajmer stands open as disciplined Ghurid soldiers march in, helmets gleaming, while a few townsfolk watch from doorways, faces unreadable.

dialogue.text: In the end, Aibak took Ajmer. The sources are brief on Hariraja’s final battle, but clear on the result: his defiance lasted about a year, then the city fell.

i18n.hi: आख़िर में ऐबक ने अजमेर ले लिया। हरिराज की आख़िरी लड़ाई पर स्रोत कम बोलते हैं, पर नतीजा साफ़ है: उसकी जिद लगभग एक साल चली, फिर शहर गिर पड़ा।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Qutb al-Din Aibak inspecting Vigraharaja’s complex, pointing for builders
panels.action: Within the temple-college courtyard, Qutb al-Din Aibak stands with architects and masons, gesturing toward the colonnades as they study the carved pillars.

dialogue.text: Hasan Nizami’s Taj-ul-Maasir describes Aibak turning a great temple at Ajmer into a mosque, rejoicing in idol-breaking and new prayer. Archaeology ties this to Vigraharaja’s Sarasvati complex.

i18n.hi: हसन निज़ामी की ताज-उल-मासिर ऐबक को अजमेर के बड़े मंदिर को मस्जिद में बदलते दिखाती है, मूरतों के तोड़ने और नई नमाज़ पर उत्सव मनाते हुए। पुरातत्त्व इसे विग्रहराज के सरस्वती परिसर से जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: close-up on a sculpted Sanskrit drama slab being pried loose by a mason’s tools
panels.action: A mason’s hand and chisel work at the edge of a large carved slab, Sanskrit lines and dramatic figures clearly visible as the stone is readied to be moved.

dialogue.text: From these halls, masons lifted inscribed slabs. The verses did not vanish; they were turned sideways, built into new walls, their scripts facing outward and inward.

i18n.hi: यहीं से राजमिस्त्री ने लेखों वाली पट्टियाँ उखाड़ीं। श्लोक मिटे नहीं; उन्हें घुमा कर नई दीवारों में जड़ दिया गया, लिपियाँ बाहर और भीतर की ओर मुँह किए।

panels.shot: wide interior view of Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra as a mosque under construction
panels.action: Under a high roof of arches, reused Hindu pillars and carved slabs form aisles, while workers raise new screens and mihrabs, scaffolding crisscrossing the space.

dialogue.text: The Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra mosque rose. The Archaeological Survey of India notes the Sanskrit drama inscriptions still embedded in its structure, witness to conversion by reuse.

i18n.hi: अढ़ाई-दिन-का-झोंपड़ा मस्जिद उठ खड़ी हुई। भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण आज भी उसके ढाँचे में धँसे संस्कृत नाटक के शिलालेख दिखाता है, जो पुनःप्रयोग से हुए रूपांतरण के गवाह हैं।

panels.shot: measured close-up of Qur’anic calligraphy side by side with faint Sanskrit on a pillar
panels.action: On a single pillar, fresh geometric carving and Arabic script share space with weathered Sanskrit letters and floral motifs, both lit by a shaft of sunlight.

dialogue.text: Hasan Nizami celebrated such acts as the ‘victory of Islam’. The stone itself shows a quieter fact: old words remained, buried in service to new rites.

i18n.hi: हसन निज़ामी ने इन कामों को ‘इस्लाम की फ़तह’ कहा। खुद पत्थर एक धीमा सच दिखाते हैं: पुराने शब्द रह गए, नई पूजा की सेवा में दबे हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of early Qutb complex at Delhi, with Qutb Minar base and mosque arches
panels.action: In Delhi, the early Qutb complex rises: mosque arches and the growing shaft of the Qutb Minar, surrounded by scaffolds and workers, on the site of older structures.

dialogue.text: Around 1193, Aibak also began the Qutb complex at Delhi. As Ajmer was reshaped, Delhi became the center of Ghurid and later Sultanate rule over former Chahamana lands.

i18n.hi: करीब ११९३ में ऐबक ने दिल्ली में क़ुतुब परिसर भी शुरू किया। जिस तरह अजमेर ढाला गया, दिल्ली ग़ुरी और बाद की सल्तनत का पूर्व चाहमान इलाक़ों पर नया केंद्र बनी।

panels.shot: muted medium interior of a Rajput court generations later, poet reciting to an attentive ruler
panels.action: In a later Rajput court, a poet sits reciting from a palm-leaf manuscript, while a king in rich garments listens intently, warriors seated behind him.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the Hammira Mahakavya told of Hariraja dying by self-immolation after defeat. Historians note this as later tradition; contemporary Ghurid records are silent on his end.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद हम्मीर महाकाव्य ने हरिराज को हार के बाद आत्मदाह से मरता बताया। इतिहासकार इसे बाद की परंपरा मानते हैं; उस समय के ग़ुरी दस्तावेज़ उसकी मौत पर ख़ामोश हैं।

panels.shot: somber close-up imagining Hariraja on a ridge overlooking Ajmer, spectral, fading into stone textures
panels.action: Hariraja is shown in quiet profile atop a rocky ridge, Ajmer spread below; his form seems to blend with the weathered stone of the landscape, hinting at memory more than flesh.

dialogue.text: Hariraja held Ajmer for one hard year, then vanished from the record. His defeat shows how quickly power can pass, while the stones of Ajmer show how deeply such passing is written.

i18n.hi: हरिराज ने अजमेर एक कड़ा साल संभाला, फिर इतिहास से गुम हो गया। उसकी हार दिखाती है कि सत्ता कितनी जल्दी पलट सकती है, और अजमेर के पत्थर दिखाते हैं कि यह पलटना कितनी गहराई से दर्ज हो जाता है।
